svg.title: Tavola disegno 1
svg.text: The project gives back to the landscape the portion subtracted from the covered surface, to balance the visual and environmental impact of the new intervention. The intention is to affirm the presence of a new light and complementary monument, not in contrast but in natural harmony.

The design adapts to the context with organic and flexible shapes. The circles containing the rooms recur as sacred and cosmological symbols. The three main circles (the three masters) and the total of ten (ten worlds), are also the leaves of the lotus flowers, which is flower and fruit together, cause and effect.

The glazed foyer contains the functions and distribution adaptable to the configuration of the three rooms: separate or single room. The space opens to the surrounding and the visual relationship with the historical villa, becoming a lantern during the evening.

The covered area may eventually extend with two complementary connecting elements: a portico towards the villa and a green ramp connecting the ground with the Foyer cover. Both elements define an intermediate place between the ancient and the contemporary, defining a courtyard garden between the villa and the new Kaikan.
